title: Capture-time grouping, metadata-driven import, and export workflows
objective: Add three production-ready photographer workflow capabilities to RapidRAW: visual capture-session grouping controlled by a minute slider, safe metadata-driven import and reorganization with a drag-and-drop pattern builder, and dynamically discovered Python or JavaScript workflows for selected exports.
context: RapidRAW is a React 19/TypeScript/Tauri 2 application with Rust responsible for filesystem, EXIF, image processing, import, and export operations.

The repository already collapses same-stem RAW/JPEG variants, renders virtualized folder header rows, imports files using a small filename/date template, and exports selected images through a cancellable parallel Rust pipeline.
Pebbles v0.8.0 is installed but this fork has not initialized .pebbles; this file is an importable plan and is not Pebbles native event data.
The repository currently has no automated frontend or Rust tests.
constraints: Use RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for every observable behavior and record RED and GREEN evidence in the active Pebbles issue.
Keep capture-session grouping separate from existing RAW/JPEG group_id semantics so ratings, tags, selection expansion, and variant badges do not change.
All import destination resolution and all subprocess execution must occur in Rust; the React frontend must not construct trusted destination paths or launch interpreters.
A .py or .js file alone in a supported workflow directory must be discoverable and runnable with safe defaults; optional metadata may enhance but must not be required.
Run scripts without a shell, with bounded input/output, explicit timeout, cancellation, canonical path checks, and a minimal environment.
Desktop workflows target Windows, macOS, and Linux. Android must hide or clearly mark unsupported workflow controls and retain a safe import path.
Preserve existing settings compatibility through serde defaults and optional TypeScript fields.
Add translations for all existing locale files whenever user-visible text is introduced.
out_of_scope: Embedding Python, Node.js, or a JavaScript engine inside RapidRAW.
Installing Python, Node.js, packages, or workflow dependencies for the user.
Sandboxing trusted local scripts strongly enough to run untrusted code; selected workflows execute with the user's OS permissions.
Changing the GPU image-processing model or exposing in-memory GPU buffers to scripts.
Cloud workflow distribution or a workflow marketplace.
success_criteria: Users can enable capture-session headers, choose a grouping gap in minutes, and see stable groups based on adjacent capture times without changing selection semantics.
Users can build filename and destination-folder patterns from metadata tokens, preview every operation and conflict, and execute a safe copy or move with an auditable result summary.
Dropping a .py or .js file into the bundled installation workflow directory or ~/.rapidraw/workflows makes it appear dynamically in the export UI when its interpreter is available.

Selected workflows receive the selected export batch through a versioned JSON contract, can run per exported image or after the complete batch, and participate in progress, cancellation, timeout, and error reporting.
Frontend tests, Rust tests, type checking, linting, formatting, i18n validation, and affected cross-platform builds pass.

title: Establish feature contracts and test foundations
description: Create the shared implementation foundation needed to deliver the three workflow features safely in a repository that currently has no automated tests. This epic defines canonical contracts, quality gates, and compatibility rules before production behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture and user-visible semantics for all three features are recorded in repository-local decisions or issue descriptions.
A frontend unit/component test command and Rust test command are available and exercised in CI.
All later feature issues can reference stable typed contracts rather than untyped any payloads.
verification: Run npm test using the newly configured frontend test runner.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml.
Run npm run typecheck and cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings.
constraints: Do not weaken existing lint, type-check, formatting, i18n, or build checks.
Prefer pure functions and temporary directories so tests do not require a running Tauri window or GPU.

title: Initialize Pebbles and import the approved issue graph
description: Initialize Pebbles with a stable rapidraw fork prefix, validate this complete pebbles-plan/v1 document before mutation, import every issue through pb commands or a validated idempotent importer, then verify hierarchy and blocker relationships. Never edit .pebbles/events.jsonl manually.
acceptance_criteria: .pebbles is initialized with a stable lowercase prefix.
Every logical key in PLAN-001 maps to exactly one Pebbles issue.
Parent-child and depends_on relationships match this plan without cycles or duplicate issues.
The derived Pebbles database is ignored while durable event JSONL state is tracked.
verification: Run pb version and record v0.8.0 or the installed version in an issue comment.
Run pb list --status open,in_progress, pb ready, and pb dep tree for each root epic.
Re-run the importer or preflight in idempotency mode and confirm no duplicate issue is created.
constraints: Validate the full plan before creating the first issue.
Resolve Pebbles IDs after parent-child operations because IDs may be renamed.
Do not close implementation issues during import.

title: Add automated frontend and Rust test foundations
description: Introduce the smallest maintainable test foundation for pure TypeScript utilities, React interaction tests, and Rust filesystem/process services. Add Vitest with Testing Library and jsdom for frontend behavior, and use Rust unit/integration tests with tempfile for native logic. Wire tests into package scripts and CI without requiring GPU initialization.
acceptance_criteria: npm test runs TypeScript utility and React component tests once in CI mode.
cargo test runs pure Rust tests without opening the app or requiring a GPU.
CI fails when either test suite fails.
A trivial failing test is observed before configuration is completed, then the same test passes after setup.
verification: Record RED for npm test before the runner/configuration exists.
Run npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run lint.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml.
Inspect .github/workflows/lint.yml and confirm both test commands are non-optional steps.
constraints: Do not introduce a second JavaScript package manager.
Do not make tests depend on production user directories or installed Python/Node executables; use fake executables where process behavior is tested.

title: Define typed cross-boundary feature contracts
description: Define canonical Rust and TypeScript boundary models for capture grouping settings, import preview/execution, metadata tokens, workflow discovery, workflow selection, progress, and results. Specify stable camelCase serialization, version fields where contracts may be consumed by scripts, and backward-compatible defaults for existing settings files.
acceptance_criteria: Every new invoke payload and event payload has a named Rust type and matching TypeScript interface.
AppSettings loads old settings JSON with defaults for all new fields.
Unknown workflow contract versions and invalid import enums fail with actionable errors.
No new feature boundary uses any in TypeScript.
verification: Run Rust serde round-trip and old-settings compatibility tests.
Run npm run typecheck and tests for representative IPC/event payload fixtures.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml typed_contracts.
constraints: Rust is the authority for filesystem plans and workflow execution.
Keep transient execution state out of persisted AppSettings.

title: Group the library into visual capture sessions
description: Add optional display-only grouping that divides the visible library into sessions based on the elapsed minutes between adjacent image capture times and renders a header for each session. The existing same-stem RAW/JPEG collapsing feature remains independent and may be enabled at the same time.
acceptance_criteria: Users can enable or disable capture-session grouping and configure its gap threshold in whole minutes.
Groups are shown as visual sections in supported library views and do not modify ImageFile.group_id.
Missing or late EXIF data, filtering, sorting, recursive folders, virtual copies, and RAW/JPEG variants behave deterministically.
Large libraries remain responsive while moving the slider.
verification: Run focused grouping utility and library component tests.
Run npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run i18n:check, and npm run build.
Execute the existing bench replay before and after the change and compare scrolling/regrouping behavior.

title: Implement and test capture-session clustering
description: Create a pure TypeScript capture-time parser and clustering function. For each image use DateTimeOriginal plus OffsetTimeOriginal/SubSecTimeOriginal when available, then CreateDate, then the existing modified timestamp as a documented fallback. Within each folder context, sort by effective capture instant and start a new session when the gap from the immediately previous image is greater than the configured threshold. Equality belongs to the current session. Return stable session IDs, start/end instants, fallback counts, and images without mutating input.
acceptance_criteria: A threshold of N minutes groups adjacent images whose gap is less than or equal to N and splits larger gaps.
The implementation parses EXIF YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS without relying on browser-dependent Date parsing.
Timezone offsets and subseconds are honored when supplied.
Images missing EXIF use modified time and are marked as fallback-derived.
Input ordering and arrays are not mutated; ties use normalized path as a stable final key.
Session IDs remain stable when unrelated images outside the session are added.
verification: Record RED tests for exact-boundary gaps, chain grouping, timezone offsets, missing metadata, ties, and invalid dates.
Run npm test -- captureTimeGrouping.
Run npm run typecheck.
constraints: Do not reuse or overwrite group_id.
Use adjacent-gap sessionization, not fixed wall-clock buckets.
Avoid adding a date library unless native parsing cannot satisfy the explicit formats.

title: Persist capture grouping controls
description: Extend AppSettings with captureTimeGroupingEnabled and captureTimeGroupingMinutes, using backward-compatible defaults of false and 15 minutes. Add an enable switch and whole-minute slider to the existing library view-options dropdown. Use a practical 1-120 minute range, display the current value, and debounce persisted writes while keeping visual updates immediate.
acceptance_criteria: Old settings load with grouping disabled and a 15-minute default.
The slider supports keyboard input and shows an accessible label containing the current minute value.
Changing the control immediately recomputes the derived view and survives restart.
Existing RAW/JPEG grouping controls retain their values and behavior.
verification: Run settings serde compatibility tests and a React control interaction test.
Run npm test -- LibraryHeader and npm run typecheck.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml app_settings.
Manually restart the application and confirm persistence.
constraints: Do not force a folder rescan for slider changes.
Do not store the slider in transient library filter state.

title: Integrate sessions into the derived library model
description: Extend the library derivation pipeline to produce explicit display sections after RAW/JPEG variant collapsing and filtering. Capture grouping requires chronological ordering within each folder; preserve the user's previous sort so it can be restored when grouping is disabled, or clearly disable incompatible sort choices while enabled. Recompute when asynchronous EXIF enrichment changes ImageFile metadata without resetting selection or scroll unnecessarily.
acceptance_criteria: Filtering and search happen before session boundaries are displayed, so headers only count visible representative images.
RAW/JPEG collapsing happens before sessionization while group badges and expanded operations still use existing group_id.
Recursive mode never merges sessions across different source folders.
Enabling grouping gives chronological sessions regardless of prior incompatible sort selection; disabling restores the prior sort.
EXIF arriving after initial render updates affected sessions deterministically without clearing selected image paths.
verification: Run derived-model tests covering filter/search, RAW/JPEG grouping, recursive folders, late EXIF, and sort restoration.
Run npm test -- useSortedLibrary captureTimeGrouping.
Manually load a folder slowly from rotational storage and observe late metadata regrouping.
constraints: Keep header rows out of ImageFile arrays used by editor navigation and batch actions.
Memoize by image metadata/settings so slider changes are linear and do not trigger native I/O.

title: Render accessible capture-session headers
description: Extend the virtualized library row model and item renderer with capture-session header rows modeled on existing recursive folder headers. Show localized start/end time, image count, and a subtle indicator when fallback filesystem timestamps are present. Support grid and list modes; in recursive mode nest session sections below folder headers. Decide explicitly whether culling mode ignores headers or provides equivalent separators and encode that behavior in tests.
acceptance_criteria: Each visible session has one non-selectable header with localized time range and count.
Grid/list keyboard navigation skips headers and still reaches every image.
Header height is included correctly in virtualization and scrolling to a selected image remains accurate.
Recursive folders show folder header followed by their own session headers without cross-folder mixing.
Empty results do not render orphan headers.
verification: Run Testing Library tests for labels, header counts, keyboard navigation, and empty state.
Run npm test -- LibraryGrid LibraryItems.
Manually test small, medium, and large thumbnail sizes in flat and recursive modes.
constraints: Do not make headers selectable or include them in export/rating/tagging path arrays.
Use fixed measurable header heights compatible with react-window.

title: Validate capture grouping performance and regressions
description: Complete capture-session grouping with regression coverage and a performance budget. Exercise large synthetic libraries, slider changes, selection, filmstrip navigation, search, advanced EXIF queries, RAW/JPEG variant actions, and asynchronous metadata updates. Document the final semantics in user-facing help or README documentation.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic 10,000-image grouping benchmark completes within an agreed interactive budget on development hardware and does not perform filesystem calls.
Selection, ratings, labels, metadata edits, exports, and filmstrip navigation target only images and preserve existing variant expansion behavior.
All locale catalogs contain the new strings.
User documentation explains adjacent-gap grouping and timestamp fallback.
verification: Run npm test and the capture grouping performance test with a documented threshold.
Run npm run format:check, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run i18n:check, and npm run build.
Run bench/replay.js according to bench/README.md and record before/after observations.
constraints: Treat a material virtualized scrolling regression as a blocker, not deferred cleanup.

title: Build safe metadata-driven image import
description: Upgrade the existing import dialog and Rust copy loop into a preview-first import planner and executor. Users can select source files or a source folder, build destination folder and filename patterns from EXIF/IPTC/XMP/timestamp properties, resolve collisions explicitly, and copy or move associated files without silent data loss.
acceptance_criteria: Every planned destination is visible before execution and generated by the same Rust resolver used during execution.
Pattern tokens cover a documented metadata catalog and can be arranged through an accessible drag-and-drop builder.
Invalid paths, collisions, duplicate destinations, missing metadata, and unsupported files are resolved or block execution before writes.
Move never deletes a source or sidecar until its destination copy is verified.
Import can be cancelled and produces a structured per-file summary.
verification: Run focused Rust tests for metadata resolution, path safety, preview planning, copy/move execution, cancellation, and source-retention failure modes.
Run frontend tests for the import pattern builder, preview, presets, progress, and result reporting.
Complete the documented cross-platform import matrix and confirm no source loss or silent overwrite.

title: Define the import metadata catalog and precedence
description: Create a normalized MetadataCatalog model for import planning. Merge existing .rrdata/.rrexif overrides, embedded EXIF/RAW metadata, and supported XMP/IPTC fields using explicit precedence. Initial tokens must include original filename/stem/extension, sequence, DateTimeOriginal date/time parts, Make, Model, LensModel, ISO, Artist, Copyright, ImageDescription, Keywords, Rating, and ColorLabel. Record raw source, normalized value, and missing status per property.
acceptance_criteria: Metadata precedence is documented and covered by tests.
EXIF/RAW extraction reuses exif_processing rather than independently reparsing in the import module.
XMP sidecars provide keywords, rating, color label, creator/artist, description/caption, headline, copyright, and location when present.
A missing token value is represented explicitly and does not become the string undefined/null.
Reading metadata does not modify source files.
verification: Record RED fixtures for JPEG EXIF, representative RAW metadata, XMP sidecar, conflicting sidecar/embedded values, and missing fields.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml metadata_catalog.
Inspect fixture licenses and ensure no private user metadata is committed.
constraints: Do not promise full arbitrary IPTC support in the first increment; expose the tested normalized catalog.
Keep metadata values bounded to prevent oversized template expansion.

title: Create a safe metadata pattern engine
description: Replace ad-hoc string replacement for import planning with a typed token sequence resolver shared where practical by import, rename, and export. Resolve folder and filename patterns separately, preserve the original extension unless explicitly configured otherwise, sanitize every generated path segment per target OS, reject absolute paths and traversal, handle Windows reserved names and trailing dots/spaces, enforce component/path length limits, and report missing token policy. Keep compatibility for existing brace templates by parsing them into token sequences.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy tokens continue to produce their prior valid names.
Folder tokens cannot escape the selected destination root through separators, absolute paths, .., device names, Unicode tricks, or symlink traversal.
Filename and folder literals preserve Unicode where legal and use deterministic replacement for illegal characters.
Missing metadata supports explicit empty, literal fallback, or blocking-error policy with a safe default.
Two sources resolving to one destination are reported as a batch conflict before execution.
The resolver output includes a human-readable list of warnings and errors.
verification: Record RED tests for traversal, absolute paths, Windows reserved names, separators, Unicode, long names, duplicate destinations, missing fields, and legacy templates.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml pattern_engine.
Run existing rename/export manual checks using all legacy tokens.
constraints: Never interpolate untrusted metadata directly into a PathBuf without segment sanitization.
Canonicalize the destination root and re-check containment immediately before writes.
Do not silently overwrite.

title: Add import source scanning and preview IPC
description: Add Rust commands to scan either selected files or a source folder, build an ImportPlan, and return paged preview rows. Each row includes source path, destination path relative to the chosen root, metadata summary, associated files, byte size, status, collision details, and warnings. Include a plan ID or immutable request hash so execution can prove it is using the previewed inputs and settings.
acceptance_criteria: Users can choose multiple source files or one source folder with optional recursive scanning.
Only supported image types enter the plan; unsupported files are counted and reported.
Preview detects existing destination collisions, intra-batch collisions, source-equals-destination, unreadable files, invalid metadata, and insufficient destination information without writing files.
Large scans emit progress, support cancellation, and return preview pages without blocking the UI.
Changing any source, destination, pattern, mode, or collision setting invalidates the old plan ID.
verification: Run Rust temporary-directory tests for file selection, recursive folder scanning, unsupported files, collisions, and plan invalidation.
Run an IPC serialization test for preview rows and progress events.
Manually preview at least 1,000 mixed files and confirm UI remains responsive.
constraints: Preview must be side-effect free.
Do not trust a destination path supplied per row by the frontend; execution uses the Rust plan.
Bound traversal depth and protect against symlink loops.

title: Build the drag-and-drop import pattern editor
description: Replace the untyped ImportSettingsModal template input with a typed import workspace. Provide categorized metadata token palettes, separate droppable folder-pattern and filename-pattern strips, draggable token/literal blocks, keyboard reorder/remove controls, literal text editing, fallback values, live validation, and a text representation for advanced users. Reuse @dnd-kit/core already present in the repository and keep click-to-insert compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Users can drag metadata tokens into folder and filename patterns and reorder or remove them.
All drag-and-drop operations have equivalent keyboard and button controls with visible focus states and accessible names.
The editor serializes to the typed pattern model and round-trips without losing literals, token options, or order.
A debounced preview refresh shows destination examples and validation errors after changes.
The start button remains disabled for blocking plan errors and explains why.
verification: Run component tests for drag insertion, keyboard reorder, literal editing, serialization round-trip, and disabled execution.
Run npm test -- ImportPatternBuilder ImportSettingsModal.
Run npm run typecheck and npm run lint.
Perform keyboard-only and screen-reader-label manual checks.
constraints: Do not duplicate the Rust path resolver in TypeScript; frontend validation is advisory and the preview command is authoritative.
Avoid HTML5 drag-only interactions.

title: Persist import presets and last-used locations
description: Add backward-compatible ImportPreset settings modeled on existing export presets. Persist named folder/filename patterns, operation mode, collision policy, missing-token policy, associated-file options, timestamp behavior, and last source/target locations. Never persist a scanned file list or transient plan ID.
acceptance_criteria: Users can create, apply, rename, and delete named import presets.
A reserved last-used preset restores safe non-destructive settings and prior locations.
Old settings files deserialize successfully and get no unexpected destructive defaults.
Applying a preset invalidates and regenerates the preview.
verification: Run Rust settings migration and serialization tests.
Run component tests for preset CRUD and preview invalidation.
Restart the app and confirm persistence.
constraints: Default operation is copy, default collision policy is rename-with-suffix or skip, and source deletion is never silently restored as enabled.
Store patterns as typed structures with a schema version.

title: Execute verified import plans safely
description: Implement execution of the immutable previewed ImportPlan. Support copy and move. Create destination directories safely, write through a temporary file in the destination directory, flush and verify byte count plus optional hash, then atomically rename where possible. Copy all selected associated .rrdata virtual-copy sidecars, .rrexif, and .xmp files using consistent renamed destinations. For move across filesystems, complete and verify all destination files before trashing sources. Remove the current fallback that permanently deletes a source when trash fails.
acceptance_criteria: Execution rejects stale or altered plan IDs and re-checks destination containment and collisions immediately before each write.
Copy leaves every source untouched and reports verified outputs.
Move deletes/trashes a source group only after every planned destination in that group is verified.
Trash failure leaves the source in place and reports a warning or failure; it never falls back to permanent deletion.
Partial failures are isolated by source group and represented accurately in the final result.
Filesystem timestamps can be preserved from source or set from capture time according to settings.
verification: Run temporary-directory integration tests for copy, same-volume move, simulated cross-volume move, sidecars, collisions appearing after preview, write failure, verification failure, and trash failure.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml import_execution.
Manually import a RAW plus .rrdata/.xmp and confirm edits and metadata survive.
constraints: No overwrite policy in the first safe increment unless it has a separate explicit confirmation and backup design.
Never delete first and copy second.
Operations must be idempotent enough to report already-completed rows after an interrupted retry.

title: Add import cancellation, progress, and result reporting
description: Replace string-only import events with typed scan, plan, copy, verify, move, and completion phases. Add an import cancellation token and command modeled on export cancellation. Present a final summary with succeeded, renamed, skipped, warned, failed, and retained-source counts plus expandable per-file errors. Refresh affected library roots only after terminal cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Cancel stops before the next destructive boundary and waits for active file operations to reach a safe state.
The UI distinguishes planning from executing and shows current source, phase, count, and bytes when known.
A batch with failures cannot end in an undifferentiated success state.
Users can copy or save a structured error summary without exposing unrelated private paths in logs.
Library refresh occurs once after completion/cancellation and includes successfully imported files.
verification: Run tests for cancel before write, during copy, before source trash, and after final output.
Run listener/store tests for every terminal state and mixed-result summary.
Manually cancel a cross-volume move and verify all source files required for recovery remain.
constraints: Cancellation is cooperative and must never create a window where source and destination are both absent.
Do not auto-reset a detailed result before the user can inspect it.

title: Complete import platform parity and documentation
description: Finish import behavior across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android. Desktop supports file and folder sources. Android retains Storage Access Framework content URI handling with only capabilities that can be honored; unsupported move/source-delete behavior is hidden. Add all locale strings and document token catalog, precedence, collision behavior, recovery, and sidecar handling.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop source and target dialogs feed the preview-first flow.
Android never displays a destructive option that its content URI implementation ignores.
Windows reserved-name/path tests pass and macOS/Linux Unicode/path tests pass in CI or documented platform checks.
All locales pass extraction/runtime validation.
Documentation accurately lists supported EXIF/IPTC/XMP fields and fallback behavior.
verification: Run npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run i18n:check, and npm run build.

Run cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check, cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml.
Run affected Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android CI builds.
Complete the documented manual import matrix.
constraints: Do not emulate unsupported Android filesystem semantics.
Document known IPTC coverage precisely rather than claiming all tags.

title: Run dynamic Python and JavaScript export workflows
description: Add a trusted-local automation system in which .py and .js files discovered from bundled installation resources and ~/.rapidraw/workflows appear in the export UI and can be selected for a batch. Rust probes Python/Node, launches scripts without a shell, passes a versioned JSON request, captures bounded results, and integrates phases with export progress and cancellation.
acceptance_criteria: A newly added valid .py or .js file appears after refresh without rebuilding the UI.
Unavailable runtimes are visible with a reason and cannot be selected.
Selected workflows receive only the selected batch and exact exported outputs.
Per-image and after-batch phases have defined ordering, cancellation, timeout, and failure semantics.
No frontend shell command can execute arbitrary paths.
verification: Run Rust discovery, protocol, runner, export-integration, cancellation, and workflow-security tests with Python and Node fixtures.
Run frontend tests for workflow discovery, selection, ordering, progress, consent, and result reporting.
Run affected Windows, macOS, and Linux builds and confirm packaged and user workflow discovery.

title: Specify the export workflow protocol and threat model
description: Define workflow protocol version 1 before writing a runner. A standalone .py or .js file is valid with defaults derived from filename and extension. Optional adjacent <script>.rapidraw.json metadata may set stable id, display name, description, phase (postImage or postBatch), order, timeoutSeconds, and onError (warn or fail). The process receives one bounded JSON request on stdin and must emit one bounded JSON result on stdout; stderr is captured as diagnostic text. Define exit-code handling, duplicate ID precedence, environment policy, cancellation, and trust warning.
acceptance_criteria: The direct-file default requires no manifest and satisfies both Python and JavaScript workflows.

postImage means the script runs after one complete output and optional mask artifacts are written while the batch is still exporting; postBatch means one invocation after all successful outputs are known.

The v1 request includes protocolVersion, runId, workflowId, phase, source path, exported path/artifacts for postImage, complete selected/exported item lists for postBatch, export settings subset, index/total, and workspace temp directory.
The v1 response defines ok, message, warnings, and produced artifact paths; malformed output and non-zero exit are distinct errors.
The threat model states that scripts are trusted local code with user permissions and are not safe for untrusted downloads.
verification: Review the protocol against one Python and one Node fixture before implementation.
Validate example request/response documents against Rust serde models.
Record an architecture decision covering defaults, optional metadata, phases, trust, and headless behavior.
constraints: Do not expose arbitrary environment secrets by default.
Do not pass command lines through cmd.exe, PowerShell, sh, or a shell plugin.
Keep protocol v1 additive and reject unsupported major versions.

title: Discover workflows and probe runtimes
description: Create a Rust workflow registry that scans the bundled Resource/workflows directory and ~/.rapidraw/workflows for regular .py and .js files, parses optional adjacent metadata, derives defaults, canonicalizes paths, and probes interpreters. Python candidates are python3 then python on Unix and py -3 then python on Windows; JavaScript uses node. Cache probes briefly and provide an explicit refresh command. User workflows override bundled workflows only when stable IDs match, with the override reported.
acceptance_criteria: Direct .py and .js files are listed with derived ID/name and default postBatch phase.
Symlinks or metadata entry paths that escape allowed roots are rejected and reported.
Duplicate IDs, invalid metadata, unsupported extensions, unreadable files, missing home/resource directories, and unavailable runtimes produce typed diagnostics without crashing discovery.
Interpreter probes use argument arrays and a short timeout and report executable/version.
Refresh returns additions, removals, availability, source root, phase, and diagnostics deterministically.
verification: Record RED Rust tests using temporary bundled/home roots and fake interpreter executables.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml workflow_discovery.
Test Windows and Unix candidate ordering through injected process/path abstractions.
constraints: Do not execute workflow contents during discovery.
Do not recursively scan unbounded directory trees; scan only the defined workflow directory level unless metadata explicitly defines a contained entry.
Do not depend on frontend tauri-plugin-shell permissions.

title: Implement the bounded workflow subprocess runner
description: Implement an injected Rust process runner for one workflow invocation. Launch the detected interpreter directly with the canonical script path, set a controlled working/temp directory, pipe the JSON request through stdin, capture stdout/stderr with strict byte limits, enforce timeout, and terminate the child process tree on cancellation or timeout. Start from a minimal documented environment plus essential PATH/home/temp values; permit explicit safe variables later rather than forwarding the full parent environment.
acceptance_criteria: Python and Node fixture scripts receive valid protocol v1 JSON and return parsed results.
Arguments containing spaces, quotes, Unicode, or shell metacharacters are passed literally and never interpreted by a shell.
Timeout, cancellation, excessive stdout/stderr, malformed JSON, non-zero exit, missing runtime, and child spawn failure return distinct typed outcomes.
A cancelled/timed-out workflow leaves no tracked child process running.
Artifact paths in responses are canonicalized and labeled external when outside the workflow temp/export roots.
verification: Run integration tests with fake Python/Node executables for success and every failure mode.
Run process-tree cancellation tests on Windows and one Unix platform.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml workflow_runner and cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings.
constraints: Never use shell=true or concatenate a command string.
Default timeout is finite, output limits are finite, and workflow concurrency is separately bounded.
Redact sensitive environment values and large script output from application logs.

title: Integrate workflow phases with the export pipeline
description: Extend ExportSettings with selected workflow IDs and integrate the runner into export_images_impl. Resolve the immutable selected registry entries before starting. For postImage workflows, run selected workflows in user-selected order after the main file, metadata, timestamps, and mask artifacts are complete; count the export item complete only after its required workflow policy finishes. After all image workers settle, invoke postBatch workflows once with successful and failed item records. Preserve existing exports when no workflows are selected.
acceptance_criteria: No-workflow export follows the existing processing and event path with no subprocess overhead beyond an empty selection check.
postImage workflows receive only fully written outputs and run in configured order for that image.
postBatch workflows start only after all image tasks settle and receive selected, successful, failed, and skipped items.
onError=warn records a warning and continues; onError=fail fails the affected image or batch with a typed reason.
Cancellation skips unstarted workflows, terminates active workflow children, and still performs ExportTaskGuard cleanup.
Headless and GUI export share the same integration service even if their workflow selection inputs differ.
verification: Run export integration tests with marker workflows proving phase timing and ordering.
Run tests for mixed image failures, workflow warn/fail policies, masks, cancellation, and no-workflow regression.
Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml export_workflow_integration.
constraints: Do not pass in-memory images to scripts in v1.
Do not allow postImage workflows to race on the same output; sequence selected workflows per image.
Bound total concurrent workflow processes independently of export render workers.

title: Add dynamic workflow multiselect to export UI
description: Add an accessible searchable multiselect section to ExportPanel advanced settings. On panel open and explicit refresh, invoke workflow discovery. Show name, language/runtime version, phase, source (bundled or user), and unavailable/invalid reason. Users can select and order multiple available workflows; selections are stored in export presets and last-used settings by stable workflow ID, while missing IDs remain visible as unavailable rather than silently disappearing.
acceptance_criteria: Discovered workflows appear without application restart after refresh.
Multiple workflows can be selected, deselected, and ordered with mouse and keyboard.
Unavailable runtime or invalid workflow entries are disabled with an actionable reason.
Export presets round-trip selected stable IDs and order.
Android hides the section or displays a localized unsupported message.
The selection sent to Rust contains IDs only; Rust resolves trusted canonical paths.
verification: Run component tests for loading, refresh, multiselect, ordering, missing IDs, disabled entries, preset round-trip, and Android behavior.
Run npm test -- ExportWorkflowSelect ExportPanel.
Run npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm run i18n:check.
Manually add/remove scripts under ~/.rapidraw/workflows while the panel is open and refresh.
constraints: A missing workflow must never be replaced by another script with the same display filename but a different stable ID.
Do not expose arbitrary script path selection in the export panel.

title: Expose workflow progress, logs, and cancellation
description: Add typed workflow lifecycle events and extend ExportState to represent rendering, writing, post-image workflow, and post-batch workflow phases. Show current workflow/image, timeout, warning count, and a bounded diagnostic summary. Ensure the existing cancel control cancels active subprocesses as well as rendering. Preserve per-image and per-workflow errors in a result detail view instead of only reporting N of M failed.
acceptance_criteria: The UI visibly distinguishes image processing from workflow execution.
Cancel during a workflow transitions through Cancelling and reaches Cancelled only after child cleanup.
Warnings do not masquerade as failure, while fail-policy outcomes produce Error or partial-failure summary.
Captured logs are bounded, redacted, and associated with workflow ID and item without flooding frontend events.
Terminal export state remains inspectable until dismissed or a new export starts.
verification: Run store/listener tests for all event sequences and stale-run event rejection.
Run integration tests that cancel sleeping Python and Node fixtures.
Manually verify progress for multiple images with both workflow phases.
constraints: Include run IDs in events so stale workflows cannot alter a later export state.
Do not stream unbounded raw stderr to React.

title: Package workflow directories and examples
description: Add the bundled workflows resource directory and align Tauri and Flatpak packaging. Ship minimal disabled-by-choice example Python and JavaScript workflows that validate stdin, write one protocol response, and perform a harmless operation such as writing a sidecar receipt in the supplied temp directory. Add templates or documentation showing direct-file defaults and optional metadata without requiring third-party packages.
acceptance_criteria: Tauri bundles the workflows directory on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
The existing Flatpak manifest references the same actual source/destination path.
Packaged discovery finds bundled examples and user discovery finds ~/.rapidraw/workflows.
Examples run with only standard Python or Node APIs and clearly state the trusted-code warning.
Bundled examples are not auto-selected or auto-executed.
verification: Build one desktop bundle and inspect resources for workflow files.
Run Flatpak manifest validation or build check where available.
Run examples through workflow_runner integration tests with available interpreters.
Run npm run tauri build on the primary development platform.
constraints: Do not bundle Python or Node.
Keep examples deterministic, offline, and free of credentials.

title: Add headless workflow selection and documentation
description: Extend the headless export CLI with repeatable --workflow <id> and --list-workflows behavior using the same discovery, protocol, runner, and error policies as the GUI. No workflows run by default in headless mode. Emit clear deterministic terminal output and non-zero status when requested IDs are missing/unavailable or fail with fail policy. Document directory locations, runtime detection, protocol examples, phases, security, timeout, cancellation limitations, and exit behavior.
acceptance_criteria: rapidraw export accepts multiple workflow IDs in order and runs them through the shared service.
rapidraw --list-workflows or the agreed command lists ID, phase, runtime availability, and source.
Missing/unavailable requested IDs fail before image export starts.
Existing CLI commands without workflow flags retain behavior.
Documentation contains working zero-dependency Python and Node examples for both phases.
verification: Run launch parser tests for repeated flags, listing, missing values, and backward compatibility.
Run headless integration tests with fake workflows and assert exit codes/output.
Execute documented commands manually on one platform.
constraints: Do not make GUI last-used workflows implicitly apply to headless exports.
Keep secrets out of examples and logs.

title: Harden workflow execution across desktop platforms
description: Complete a security-focused and cross-platform validation pass for workflow discovery and execution. Cover canonical path containment, symlink/reparse-point escape, interpreter replacement between probe and spawn, environment leakage, path quoting, process-tree cleanup, output exhaustion, timeout, duplicate IDs, malformed metadata, and packaging paths. Remove frontend shell execution permissions if no remaining feature needs them, or scope them narrowly and document why they remain.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests cover hostile filenames/metadata and process failure modes on Windows plus at least one Unix platform.
Discovery and spawn revalidate canonical script identity sufficiently to prevent simple path substitution escapes.
No test secret placed in the parent environment appears in child output unless explicitly allowlisted.
Timeout and cancel leave no child or known descendant process alive.
Tauri capabilities expose no broader process execution to the frontend than required.
The user-facing trust warning appears before first workflow execution and records consent.
verification: Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml workflow_security.
Run cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings.
Run Windows, macOS, and Linux CI builds and workflow tests.
Review src-tauri/capabilities/default.json and confirm the minimum permission set.
constraints: Do not claim arbitrary-script sandboxing.
Treat process escape or source deletion risk as release blockers.

title: Integrate and prepare the feature proposal
description: Validate the three features together, document user workflows and architecture, and prepare small reviewable upstream proposal branches or pull requests. Keep each feature independently mergeable and avoid unrelated refactoring.
acceptance_criteria: All three features coexist without changing existing editing/export/import defaults.
The full local quality gate and affected CI matrix pass.
Architecture, security, compatibility, screenshots, and manual test evidence are ready for upstream review.
Changes are split into reviewable proposals with clear Pebbles issue references.
verification: Run the complete frontend and Rust quality gates and all affected cross-platform CI builds.
Complete the end-to-end workflow regression matrix and review documentation against implemented behavior.
Inspect each proposed change set from a clean checkout and run its stated test plan.

title: Run end-to-end workflow regression matrix
description: Run a combined regression matrix using representative JPEG, RAW, RAW+JPEG, .rrdata, .rrexif, and XMP fixtures. Import through metadata patterns, browse using capture-session grouping, select grouped images, export with post-image and post-batch workflows, cancel at each phase, restart, and repeat on supported desktop platforms. Verify no source loss, correct selected paths, stable settings, sidecar preservation, and cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: The complete happy path works on Windows, macOS, and Linux or has documented CI evidence for each.
Cancellation at scan, import copy, source retirement, image export, post-image workflow, and post-batch workflow leaves recoverable state.
RAW/JPEG grouping and capture-session grouping together export exactly the user-selected logical paths according to existing variant semantics.
No workflow runs unless selected and consented; no move deletes an unverified source.
Performance remains acceptable for a documented large-library/import/export fixture.
verification: Run npm test, npm run format:check, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run i18n:check, and npm run build.

Run cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check, cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml.
Run the documented manual matrix and attach logs/screenshots to the Pebbles issue.
Run affected multi-platform CI builds.
constraints: Do not use private photographs or personal metadata as committed fixtures.
Any data-loss, path-escape, or orphan-process failure blocks release.

title: Document architecture and user workflows
description: Write focused documentation for capture-session grouping, import patterns and recovery, and export script workflows. Include diagrams only where they clarify boundaries, exact folder locations by platform, token and metadata tables, protocol JSON, example scripts, runtime troubleshooting, trust warnings, and migration/default behavior. Update README feature summaries without claiming unimplemented capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can configure each feature from documentation without reading source code.
A simpler implementation agent can locate canonical modules, contracts, commands, tests, and safety invariants.
Workflow documentation distinguishes trusted code execution from sandboxing and explains interpreter discovery.
Import documentation explains preview, collision, verification, move recovery, metadata precedence, and sidecar behavior.
Capture grouping documentation explains adjacent-gap semantics and timestamp fallback.
verification: Run documentation link checks if available and manually execute every documented command/example.
Run npm run i18n:check for linked UI labels.
Review docs against actual settings defaults and file locations on all desktop platforms.
constraints: Do not duplicate volatile active-work status in documentation.
Mark optional/future behavior clearly.

title: Prepare reviewable upstream proposals
description: Split the completed work into independently reviewable proposals: test/contracts foundation, capture-session grouping, import planner/executor, and export workflows. Each proposal must explain user value, compatibility defaults, security implications, screenshots, performance evidence, and exact verification. Rebase or merge upstream safely without rewriting shared history.
acceptance_criteria: Each proposal is coherent, builds independently at its boundary, and references its Pebbles issues.
No proposal mixes unrelated formatting or generated artifacts.
The import proposal explicitly calls out changed deletion safety; the workflow proposal explicitly calls out trusted arbitrary code execution.
Upstream feedback and CI findings are captured as new Pebbles issues rather than buried in comments.
verification: Inspect git diff and commit range for each proposal against its intended base.
Run each proposal's stated test plan from a clean checkout.
Confirm repository status and Pebbles durable events are committed with their related changes when commits are requested.
constraints: Do not push or open pull requests without explicit user authorization.
Never force-push main/master.
